categories.label: Solved
categories.description: Answered, and the answer is accepted (source of record, refereed publication, or broad expert acceptance).

categories.label: AI proposed
categories.description: An AI system produced a claimed full solution that mathematicians have not yet confirmed. Treated as unsolved until confirmed.

categories.label: Partial
categories.description: An explicitly stated part of the problem is answered; the rest remains open.

categories.label: Open
categories.description: No accepted answer. Partial results, human claims under review, and AI partial results are shown as badges.

ai-partial.label: AI partial result
ai-partial.description: An AI system produced a result on a part, special case or variant; it does not answer the whole problem.

ai-confirmed.label: AI solution confirmed
ai-confirmed.description: The source of record accepted a solution produced by an AI system after expert checking.

ai-assisted-solution.label: AI-assisted solution
ai-assisted-solution.description: The accepted solution was produced with substantial help from an AI system.

human-claim.label: Claim under review
human-claim.description: A human-authored claimed solution has not yet been accepted.

lean-pending.label: Lean proof awaiting review
lean-pending.description: A Lean proof is published upstream but has not been reviewed by people; not re-checked by this server.

withdrawn-claim.label: Withdrawn claim
withdrawn-claim.description: A claimed solution was withdrawn by its authors; withdrawn claims never count.

disputed.label: Disputed
disputed.description: A published claim or its formalization is publicly disputed.

sources-conflict.label: Sources disagree
sources-conflict.description: Sources disagree about the status; the source of record decides the category.

prize.label: Prize
prize.description: A prize is attached to this problem.

ambiguous-statement.label: Ambiguous statement
ambiguous-statement.description: The intended statement is uncertain or open to interpretation.

not-in-current-edition.label: Not in current edition
not-in-current-edition.description: The current edition of the source no longer lists this problem; the entry is kept for its links and discussion.

formal-statement.label: Lean statement
formal-statement.description: A Lean statement of the problem exists (a statement, not a proof).

upstream-substatus.label: Upstream sub-status
upstream-substatus.description: The source of record lists the problem as open with a sub-status, shown as the label (from source_status).

reported-signal.label: New report (unreviewed)
reported-signal.description: Matched automatically from primary sources; not reviewed; does not change the category.

category_rules.S1: Source-of-record marker: the source that maintains the problem lists it as answered.
category_rules.S2: Refereed or broadly accepted full answer.
category_rules.A1: Source marker: the maintainers flag an unconfirmed AI-produced solution of the whole problem.
category_rules.A2: Documented AI-produced full claim that has not been confirmed.
category_rules.P1: Source marker on an explicitly stated part.
category_rules.P2: Accepted answer to an explicitly stated part.

status_method: Each entry has exactly one category, checked in order: Solved (S1 source-of-record marker: teorth proved/disproved/solved/independent, a Kourovka ∗ before the number, the Clay Solved listing; S2 refereed or broadly accepted full answer), AI proposed (A1 a Kourovka ♯ on the whole problem; A2 a documented AI-produced full claim not yet confirmed), Partial (P1 a Kourovka ∗ on a part; P2 an accepted answer to an explicitly stated part), otherwise Open. Withdrawn or refuted claims never count. Source-of-record markers come from deterministic parsers of pinned inputs; other categories come from deep research from primary sources (October 2026, AI-assisted, with a verification pass) or committed operator decisions; research can only mark an entry solved with a refereed, maintainer-accepted or broadly accepted full answer and never asserts a source marker. Badges add partial results, claims under review, AI involvement, Lean status, prizes and conflicts between sources. The live overlay changes categories only on deterministic source changes.
status_note: Categories come from the sources of record and reviewed research; model output is never a certificate. AI proposed is never counted as solved. Lean results upstream are not re-checked by this server.
content_note: Original statements and sourced evidence for researched entries; other entries are bibliographic pointers with source markers. No problem text from the Kourovka Notebook, erdosproblems.com or Wikipedia is reproduced.

rating_method.name: Exploration fit
rating_method.author: Ansätze · AI-assisted editorial heuristic
rating_method.meaning: How concrete a starting point the available metadata offers for agent-assisted exploration. Higher means a more explicit experimental target; it does not predict a solution, mathematical difficulty, or importance.
rules: 1: A broad Millennium problem; narrow a special case before experimenting.
2: A bibliographic question requiring the original statement and literature first.
3: An explicit finite target whose basic verification proxy exceeds the stated threshold.
4: An explicit finite target within the verification threshold.
5: Level 4 with published integer bounds one apart; a precise target, not evidence that solving it is easy.
rating_method.limitations: Verification proxies ignore construction/search cost, structure, solver choice, and literature. A one-unit gap can remain exceptionally difficult. Uninspected prose problems receive 2/5, with low confidence; this is a metadata limitation, not a judgment of their value.

problems.title: Erdős #3 · divergent reciprocal sums and arithmetic progressions
problems.summary: Must every set of positive integers with divergent reciprocal sum contain arithmetic progressions of every finite length?
problems.status_headline: Still listed as open (prize $5000). OpenAI's openai/math release (Oct 2026) claims a proof via quasipolynomial Szemerédi bounds, with a Lean proof of the qualitative statement; not yet reviewed.

status_evidence.title: teorth/erdosproblems data/problems.yaml record for #3 (status: open)
status_evidence.note: The Erdős problems database lists #3 with status 'open' at commit 48e0c21 (identical to main on 2026-10-11).

status_evidence.title: Quasipolynomial Bounds for Arithmetic Progressions (openai/math family 159, manuscript dated 23 Sep 2026)
status_evidence.note: AI-produced manuscript claiming r_k(N) ≤ C_k N exp(-c_k (log N)^{eps_k}) for each k≥3, which implies the conjecture. About 198 pages; not peer reviewed.

status_evidence.title: openai/math Lean scope note for family 159 (Comparator: ErdosReciprocal.lean)
status_evidence.note: The Lean comparator statement is the qualitative reciprocal-sum conjecture; the paper's quantitative bound is outside it. Statement fidelity not yet independently reviewed.

status_evidence.title: T. Bloom, 'Erdős problems in the OpenAI proofs' (blog, 8 Oct 2026)
status_evidence.note: Lists #3 among the OpenAI claims, stresses they are unverified, and notes the Lean code appears to prove only a weaker (log log) bound, still enough for the qualitative conjecture.

statement.text: If $A\subseteq\mathbb{N}_{>0}$ and $\sum_{a\in A}1/a$ diverges, must $A$ contain nonconstant arithmetic progressions of every finite length?

sources.label: Erdős Problems · original problem and discussion

partial_results.title: Three-term progressions
partial_results.text: Bloom and Sisask proved that the divergent-reciprocal-sum hypothesis forces a nontrivial three-term arithmetic progression. This settles that length, not the conjecture for arbitrary finite lengths.

partial_results.text: Bloom and Sisask proved the k=3 case; Kelley and Meka later gave much stronger bounds for r_3(N).

statement.text: Call an infinite $A\subseteq\mathbb{N}$ admissible if no distinct $a,b,c\in A$ satisfy $a<b$, $a<c$ and $a\mid b+c$. statement.text: Let $A\subseteq\mathbb{R}$ be infinite. problems.title: Kourovka 1.3 · Zero divisors in integral group rings
problems.summary: Can two nonzero elements of an integral group ring multiply to zero when the group is torsion-free?
problems.status_headline: Open. OpenAI's openai/math release claims a torsion-free group with zero divisors in F_2[G] (Kaplansky over F_2); this does not settle the integral question.

status_evidence.claimant: E. I. Khukhro, V. D. Mazurov (editors)
status_evidence.title: Kourovka Notebook No. 21 (arXiv 1401.0300v48)
status_evidence.note: 1.3 is unmarked (unsolved) in the October 2026 edition.

status_evidence.title: A Torsion-Free Group Algebra with Zero Divisors
status_evidence.note: Claims a finitely presented torsion-free G with zero divisors in F_2[G]; characteristic-two cancellation, no claim for Z[G].

statement.text: Let $G$ be a torsion-free group: no element other than its identity has finite order. Must $\alpha\beta\ne0$ hold whenever $\alpha$ and $\beta$ are nonzero elements of the integral group ring $\mathbb{Z}[G]$? Elements of $\mathbb{Z}[G]$ are finite integer linear combinations of group elements, multiplied using the group law.

sources.label: Kourovka Notebook No. 21, problem 1.3 (arXiv:1401.0300v48, October 2026), page 5

partial_results.title: Ordered groups
partial_results.text: The answer is yes for right-orderable groups, hence for locally indicable groups. The group-algebra theorem over a field also gives the integral case by embedding ℤ[G] in ℚ[G].

sources.label: Linnell, Analytic versions of the zero divisor conjecture, Theorems 4.1 and 4.6

partial_results.title: Elementary amenable groups
partial_results.text: Kropholler, Linnell and Moody established the zero-divisor conclusion for torsion-free elementary amenable groups, a class containing all solvable groups. Linnell’s Theorem 4.6 includes integer coefficients directly.

sources.label: Linnell, Analytic versions of the zero divisor conjecture, Theorems 4.1 and 4.6

partial_results.title: The related unit conjecture is different
partial_results.text: Gardam disproved the unit conjecture over the two-element field. His example still satisfies the zero-divisor conjecture; it does not answer Kourovka 1.3 negatively.

sources.label: Gardam, A counterexample to the unit conjecture for group rings

problems.detail_note: Listed in the first Kourovka issue (1965), submitted as a well-known problem by L. A. Bokut’. This is the integral-coefficient form of the zero-divisor conjecture.
problems.source_status: Listed without an answer marker in the October 2026 edition (arXiv:1401.0300v48)

status_evidence.title: The McKay Conjecture on character degrees
status_evidence.note: Received 2024-07-31, accepted 2025-04-17. Verifies the inductive McKay condition for simple groups, finishing the 2007 Isaacs–Malle–Navarro reduction.

statement.text: For every finite group $G$ and prime $p$, let $P$ be a Sylow $p$-subgroup of $G$. Then $G$ and $N_G(P)$ have the same number of irreducible complex characters whose degree is not divisible by $p$: $|\mathrm{Irr}_{p'}(G)|=|\mathrm{Irr}_{p'}(N_G(P))|$.

problems.title: Birch and Swinnerton-Dyer conjecture
problems.summary: Relate the rank of an elliptic curve over the rationals to its L-function at s = 1.
problems.status_headline: Open. OpenAI's openai/math (Oct 2026) claims full BSD for Selmer corank ≤ 1 curves (special case); unreviewed.

status_evidence.title: The Millennium Prize Problems (BSD under 'Unsolved problems')
Exact Birch–Swinnerton-Dyer formula from low Selmer corank
status_evidence.note: Claims full BSD leading-term formula for every E/Q whose q-power Selmer corank is 0 or 1 for some prime q; with family 006, density-one of twists. Not the general conjecture.

statement.text: For an elliptic curve $E/\mathbb{Q}$, is $\operatorname{rank}E(\mathbb{Q})=\operatorname{ord}_{s=1}L(E,s)$? The full Birch–Swinnerton-Dyer conjecture also predicts the leading coefficient using the regulator, periods, Tamagawa factors, torsion and the Tate–Shafarevich group. The linked official formulation fixes the complete target.

partial_results.title: Analytic rank zero and one
partial_results.text: Gross–Zagier and Kolyvagin establish the rank equality when the analytic rank is $0$ or $1$, together with finiteness of the Tate–Shafarevich group in these cases. These results do not establish the full leading-coefficient formula for all elliptic curves.

partial_results.title: Analytic rank zero and one
partial_results.text: Gross–Zagier and Kolyvagin establish the rank equality when the analytic rank is $0$ or $1$, with finiteness of the Tate–Shafarevich group in these cases.

partial_results.title: Positive proportion of rank zero
partial_results.text: Bhargava and Shankar show that, when curves over $\mathbb{Q}$ are ordered by height, those of rank $0$ make up a positive proportion.

problems.title: Williamson conjecture
problems.summary: Call four symmetric circulant $n\times n$ matrices $A,B,C,D$ with entries $\pm1$ Williamson matrices if $A^2+B^2+C^2+D^2=4nI_n$; they assemble into a Hadamard matrix of order $4n$. Williamson's conjecture asserted that Williamson matrices exist for every positive integer $n$.
problems.source_locator: Wikipedia · List of unsolved problems in mathematics › Algebra (revision 1379514120, entry wpu-012)
problems.status_headline: Solved (disproved). Đoković (1993) found no Williamson matrices of order 35; orders 47, 53, 59 also fail. Existence for all even orders remains open.

status_evidence.title: Williamson matrices of order 4n for n = 33, 35, 39
status_evidence.note: Exhaustive computer search shows no Williamson matrices exist for n = 35, refuting existence for all n.

status_evidence.claimant: Curtis Bright, Ilias Kotsireas, Vijay Ganesh
status_evidence.title: A SAT+CAS Method for Enumerating Williamson Matrices of Even Order
status_evidence.note: Enumerates even orders n < 65 (all exist); recalls nonexistence at 35, 47, 53, 59; supports the open even-order question.

statement.text: Call four symmetric circulant $n\times n$ matrices $A,B,C,D$ with entries $\pm1$ Williamson matrices if $A^2+B^2+C^2+D^2=4nI_n$; they assemble into a Hadamard matrix of order $4n$. Williamson's conjecture asserted that Williamson matrices exist for every positive integer $n$. (A remaining open refinement asks whether they exist for every even $n$.)

problems.title: Lander's conjecture
problems.summary: Let $D$ be a $(v,k,\lambda)$ difference set in an abelian group $G$ of order $v$, with order $n=k-\lambda$. Lander (1983) conjectured that whenever some prime $p$ divides $\gcd(v,n)$, the Sylow $p$-subgroup of $G$ is non-cyclic.

statement.text: Let $D$ be a $(v,k,\lambda)$ difference set in an abelian group $G$ of order $v$, with order $n=k-\lambda$. Lander (1983) conjectured that whenever some prime $p$ divides $\gcd(v,n)$, the Sylow $p$-subgroup of $G$ is non-cyclic. It implies Ryser's conjecture on cyclic difference sets and hence the circulant Hadamard conjecture.

problems.summary: A Barker sequence of length $n$ is $a_1,\dots,a_n\in\{+1,-1\}$ whose aperiodic autocorrelations satisfy $\bigl|\sum_{i=1}^{n-k}a_ia_{i+k}\bigr|\le1$ for $1\le k<n$. Conjecture: no Barker sequence has length $n>13$.

statement.text: A Barker sequence of length $n$ is $a_1,\dots,a_n\in\{+1,-1\}$ whose aperiodic autocorrelations satisfy $\bigl|\sum_{i=1}^{n-k}a_ia_{i+k}\bigr|\le1$ for $1\le k<n$. Conjecture: no Barker sequence has length $n>13$. Odd lengths were settled by Turyn and Storer (1961); an even-length one with $n>4$ would give a circulant Hadamard matrix of order $n$, so the open case is even $n>4$.

problems.title: Hadamard's maximal determinant problem
problems.summary: For each $n\ge1$ determine $D(n)=\max\{|\det M| : M\in\{-1,1\}^{n\times n}\}$ (equivalently, $D(n)/2^{n-1}$ is the largest determinant of an $(n-1)\times(n-1)$ matrix with entries in $\{0,1\}$).
problems.source_locator: Wikipedia · List of unsolved problems in mathematics › Algebra (revision 1379514120, entry wpu-016)
problems.status_headline: Open. Exact maxima known only for small orders and special families; 2026 preprints report new record determinants for some orders n ≡ 3 (mod 4).

status_evidence.title: New Records for the Hadamard Maximal Determinant Problem
status_evidence.note: Record determinants for n = 51 and n ≡ 3 (mod 4) with 103 ≤ n ≤ 119 (v3 Oct 2026); optimality shown only within a circulant-block family; learning-based and annealing searches.

statement.text: For each $n\ge1$ determine $D(n)=\max\{|\det M| : M\in\{-1,1\}^{n\times n}\}$ (equivalently, $D(n)/2^{n-1}$ is the largest determinant of an $(n-1)\times(n-1)$ matrix with entries in $\{0,1\}$). Hadamard's inequality gives $D(n)\le n^{n/2}$, with equality exactly when a Hadamard matrix of order $n$ exists; the exact value is unknown for infinitely many $n$.

statement.text: A family of conjectures on Noetherian local rings, chiefly due to Hochster, Serre, Auslander, Bass and Peskine–Szpiro. Main members: the direct summand conjecture (a regular ring splits off every module-finite extension), existence of big Cohen–Macaulay algebras, the monomial and canonical element conjectures, existence of a small (finitely generated maximal) Cohen–Macaulay module over every complete local domain, and Serre's positivity $\chi(M,N)>0$ for modules over a regular local ring with $\ell(M\otimes N)<\infty$ and $\dim M+\dim N=\dim R$.

sources.label: André, La conjecture du facteur direct, Publ. Math. IHÉS 127 (2018)
Dospinescu, La conjecture du facteur direct (d'après Y. André et B. Bhatt), Séminaire Bourbaki

problems.title: Jacobson's conjecture

statement.text: Collection of conjectures of I. Kaplansky. Group rings: for a field $K$ and torsion-free group $G$, (i) $K[G]$ has no zero divisors; (ii) its only idempotents are $0$ and $1$; (iii) every unit is trivial, $u=\lambda g$ with $\lambda\in K^\times$, $g\in G$. Also: every homomorphism from $C(X)$ ($X$ compact Hausdorff) to a Banach algebra is continuous; finite $u$-invariants of fields are powers of $2$; and ten conjectures on Hopf algebras.

statement.text: Köthe (1930): in every associative ring $R$, is the sum of two nil left ideals again a nil left ideal? statement.text: The Dedekind number $M(n)$ is the number of monotone Boolean functions of $n$ variables, equivalently the number of antichains in the power set of an $n$-element set (so $M(0)=2$, $M(1)=3$, $M(2)=6$). Exact values are known for $n\le 9$. Compute $M(n)$ exactly for $n\ge10$.

statement.text: For $s,t\ge 2$ let $R(s,t)$ be the least $N$ such that every red/blue colouring of the edges of $K_N$ has a red $K_s$ or a blue $K_t$. statement.text: Let $c_n$ be the number of $n$-step self-avoiding walks from the origin on a lattice such as $\mathbb Z^2$. No formula for $c_n$ is known. statement.text: Arnold conjecture: on a closed symplectic manifold $(M,\omega)$, a Hamiltonian diffeomorphism $\varphi$ has at least as many fixed points as a smooth function on $M$ must have critical points (Morse number if $\varphi$ is nondegenerate); the homological form asks $\#\mathrm{Fix}(\varphi)\ge\sum_i\dim H_i(M;\mathbb F)$. Arnold–Givental: if $L=\mathrm{Fix}(\tau)$ for an anti-symplectic involution $\tau$ and $\varphi(L)\pitchfork L$, then $\#(\varphi(L)\cap L)\ge\dim H_*(L;\mathbb F_2)$.

partial_results.title: Fukaya–Ono: rational homological Arnold conjecture
partial_results.text: The nondegenerate fixed-point count is bounded below by the sum of rational Betti numbers on every closed symplectic manifold.

statement.text: Let $M^n$ ($n\ge2$) be a Cartan–Hadamard manifold, i.e. complete, simply connected, with sectional curvature $\le 0$. Is it true that every bounded domain $\Omega\subset M$ with smooth boundary has $|\partial\Omega|\ge|\partial B|$, where $B\subset\mathbb{R}^n$ is a Euclidean ball with $|B|=|\Omega|$, with equality only when $\Omega$ is isometric to $B$? The generalized form uses a curvature bound $\kappa\le0$ and balls in the model space of curvature $\kappa$.

status_evidence.title: A Human Audit of OpenAI's AI-Generated Mathematical Proofs
status_evidence.note: Audits 18 reviews of the Aug 2026 report: no confirmed substantive error in a principal result, but a specialist review of Ch. 8 (Ehrhart) asks for major revision of compressed analytic arguments.

statement.text: Let $K\subset\mathbb{R}^n$ be a convex body whose barycenter is the origin and such that the origin is the only point of $\mathbb{Z}^n$ in the interior of $K$. Ehrhart conjectured that $\mathrm{vol}(K)\le (n+1)^n/n!$, the volume of the centered dilate $(n+1)\Delta_n-(1,\dots,1)$ of the standard simplex. (A further refinement asks that equality occur only for unimodular images of this simplex.)

statement.text: For a lattice $L\subset\mathbb{R}^n$ of covolume 1, let $\lambda_1(L)$ be the length of a shortest nonzero vector. statement.text: For a knot type $K$, the ropelength $L(K)$ is the infimum, over closed curves $C$ of type $K$, of $\operatorname{length}(C)/D(C)$, where the thickness $D(C)$ is the largest diameter of an embedded normal tube around $C$ (twice its normal injectivity radius). Is there a general formula for $L(K)$, or even an exact value for a single nontrivial knot? None is known even for the trefoil: every nontrivial knot has $L(K)\ge15.66$, while numerically tightened trefoils reach about $16.37$.

statement.text: Does there exist a polyhedron in $\mathbb{R}^3$ without self-intersections that has $f>7$ faces and in which every two faces share exactly one edge? The tetrahedron ($f=4$) and the Szilassi polyhedron ($f=7$) are the only known examples. If exactly three faces meet at each vertex, Euler's formula forces genus $(f-3)(f-4)/12$, so $f\equiv0,3,4,7\pmod{12}$ and the next candidate has $f=12$ and genus $6$.

statement.text: (Chetwynd–Hilton, 1986.) Call $H\subseteq G$ $\Delta(G)$-overfull if $|E(H)|>\Delta(G)\lfloor |V(H)|/2\rfloor$. problems.title: Main gap conjecture (extensions)
problems.summary: For a complete first-order theory $T$ in a countable language, Shelah's main gap theorem gives a dichotomy: either $I(T,\aleph_\alpha)=2^{\aleph_\alpha}$ for every $\alpha>0$, or models of $T$ are determined by well-founded trees of dimension invariants and…

statement.text: For a complete first-order theory $T$ in a countable language, Shelah's main gap theorem gives a dichotomy: either $I(T,\aleph_\alpha)=2^{\aleph_\alpha}$ for every $\alpha>0$, or models of $T$ are determined by well-founded trees of dimension invariants and $I(T,\aleph_\alpha)<\beth_{\omega_1}(|\alpha|)$ for all $\alpha>0$. The open problem is to prove an analogous dichotomy in other settings, notably for first-order theories in uncountable languages, for abstract elementary classes, and for the $\aleph_1$-saturated models of a fixed countable theory.

statement.text: A positive integer $n$ is idoneal if every genus of primitive positive definite binary quadratic forms of discriminant $-4n$ consists of a single class (equivalently, $n\neq ab+bc+ca$ for all integers $0<a<b<c$). problems.status_headline: Open in general (thin-set form). Proved for many special classes; the original Zariski-open version was disproved in 1996.

statement.text: Let $V$ be a smooth Fano variety over a number field $K$ with $V(K)$ Zariski dense, and let $H$ be an anticanonical height. Manin's conjecture, in its current form, predicts a thin subset $Z\subset V(K)$ such that $\#\{x\in V(K)\setminus Z: H(x)\le B\}\sim c\,B(\log B)^{\rho-1}$ as $B\to\infty$, where $\rho$ is the rank of $\operatorname{Pic}V$ and $c>0$ is Peyre's constant. The original 1989 form removed only a proper Zariski-closed subset, and that form fails in general.

problems.summary: Let $p$ be a complex polynomial of degree $n\ge2$ with all zeros in the closed unit disc. Sendov: does every zero $a$ of $p$ have a zero of $p'$ within distance $1$? Phelps–Rodriguez: is that distance in fact $<1$ unless $p$ is a scalar multiple of $z^n-a^n$ with $|a|=1$?

status_evidence.note: Completes the Mazur–Tao scalar reduction with less computer assistance; builds on their argument, so not an independent proof.

An (arXiv 2609.04246) completes the Mazur–Tao reduction and is not independent.

u$ be the set of sums $\sum_{s\in S}\chi(s)$ over irreducible characters $\chi$ of degree $

u=M^T_
u$ for all $
u$, i.e. is every finite group a BI-group?

problems.summary: Let $J_{s,k}(X)$ count integer solutions of $\sum_{i=1}^{s}(x_i^j-y_i^j)=0$ for $1\le j\le k$ with $1\le x_i,y_i\le X$. For all $s,k\ge1$ and $\varepsilon>0$, is $J_{s,k}(X)\ll_{s,k,\varepsilon}X^{\varepsilon}\,(X^{s}+X^{2s-k(k+1)/2})$?

problems.title: Sensitivity conjecture
problems.summary: Is there an absolute constant $C$ such that every Boolean function $f:\{0,1\}^n\to\{0,1\}$ satisfies $\deg(f)\le s(f)^{C}$ (equivalently $bs(f)\le s(f)^C$), where $s$ is sensitivity, $bs$ block sensitivity and $\deg$ real polynomial degree?
problems.source_locator: Wikipedia · Problems solved since 2015 › Theoretical computer science (revision 1379514120, entry wps-042)
problems.status_headline: Solved (true). Hao Huang (2019, Annals of Mathematics) showed every induced subgraph on 2^{n-1}+1 hypercube vertices has max degree ≥ sqrt(n), giving deg(f) ≤ s(f)^2.

status_evidence.title: Induced subgraphs of hypercubes and a proof of the Sensitivity Conjecture
status_evidence.note: Sharp sqrt(n) bound for induced subgraphs of the cube; implies sensitivity and degree are polynomially related.
